Welcome to Firle Church of England Primary School
‘I am come that they may have life,and that they may have it more abundantly’
John Chapter 10 Verse 10
A Warm Welcome to Firle Church of England Primary School
Welcome to Firle Church of England Primary School, a small and friendly school where children are encouraged to grow in confidence, discover their strengths and experience success.
Our wonderful children, dedicated staff, supportive families and strong community come together to create a special place where everyone is valued and every child is given the opportunity to grow.
Nestled in the beautiful village of Firle, near Lewes, our school is surrounded by the stunning Sussex countryside. We are fortunate to have extensive grounds, with access to a local nature reserve, allotments and the South Downs, providing an inspiring environment for learning, exploration and adventure.
As part of the Oak Tree Foundation, we work closely with Laughton Community Primary School, sharing resources, planning, skills and expertise. This partnership gives our children the benefits of being part of a wider learning community, while retaining the small and friendly feel of our small school.
Rachel WestExecutive Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Firle Church of England Primary School - Our Local Church
pageCache.text:
Christian Distinctiveness
Our Local Church
There has been a church in Firle since Saxon times. The first vicar here was in 1197 when the right to appoint a vicar passed in to the hands of the Dean and Chapter of Chichester. The church you see now is an early 13th century one with chancel, nave and West tower. It was expanded in the 14th century by replacing the North and South walls with the arches which you now see and the building of the North and South aisles. The South porch was added soon after.The chancel was fairly heavily Victorianised, with new East window and aisle windows. The Gage Chapel was built in there in of Elizabeth I. In the Gage Chapel you will find three altar tombs designed and installed in 1595. One has magnificent alabaster recumbent effigies of Sir John Gage KG and his wife Philippa, plus heraldic brasses. The other two have brass effigies and heraldry. The tombs were done by Garat Johnson and the drawing of works are at Firle Place. Sir John Gage was Constable of the Tower of London and Chacellor of the Duchy of Lancaster at the time of Henry VIII. In 1985 a new stained glass window, designed by John Piper and executed by David Wasley, was installed in the vestry as a memorial tribute to the sixth Viscount Gage.The design was inspired by William Blake's drawing in his edition of The Book of Job and by the vision in The Revelation of St John (22.2) of "the tree of life" - "Ferle" means "Oak". It is best seen on a bright morning with the Eastern sun shining through.Rev. Peter Owen Jones is our present vicar.

Class Pages
Welcome to Beech Class!
Our PE / Forest School days are Wednesdays and Fridays
🏠 Home Learning
There are lots of simple ways you can support your child's learning at home. Little and often is best. Regular reading, practising number facts and times tables, and talking about what your child is learning in school can make a real difference.
📚 Reading
We encourage children to read regularly at home, ideally for around 10–15 minutes each day.
Try asking questions to deepend their understanding such as:
Reading their school reading book
Reading comics, magazines or children's non-fiction
Listening to an adult read
Talking about what they have read
What has happened so far?
What do you think will happen next?
What does this word mean?
✏️ Spelling and Writing
Children can support their writing skills at home by:
Encourage children to say their sentence aloud before writing it and reread their work afterwards to check that it makes sense.
Our writing mantra is 'Think it, say it, write it, check it.'
Looking out for interesting words when reading
Practising handwriting
🔢 Maths
Regular practice of key number facts helps children become quicker and more confident mathematicians.
Useful things to practise include:
Even a few minutes of practice regularly can help.
2, 5 and 10 times tables
3, 4 and 8 times tables
Number bonds
Mental addition and subtraction
Telling the time
Related division facts
Number bonds and mental calculation
Telling the time
Using maths in everyday situations
💻 Useful Learning Websites
🎸 Times Tables Rock Stars
A fun way to practise times tables and related division facts and build speed, fluency and confidence. Children can play through a browser or the app using their school login.
👉 Play Times Tables Rock Stars
Little and often is best. Even 5–10 minutes of regular practice can be a useful part of your child's home-learning routine.
🌳 Oak National Academy
Free lessons and activities covering English, maths and other curriculum subjects. There are separate Year 3 and Year 4 materials, so this works particularly well for a mixed-age class. Oak describes its KS2 maths and English curricula as National Curriculum aligned. [thenational.academy], [thenational.academy]
https://www.thenational.academy/
📺 BBC Bitesize
Games, videos, explanations and activities covering a wide range of KS2 subjects. BBC Bitesize is also listed as a KS2 resource for subjects including English, geography, history and computing. [familyinfo...ire.gov.uk]
https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/levels/zbr9wmn
🗺️ National Geographic Kids
A great resource for curious learners, particularly for geography, science and the wider world. It includes activities and quizzes suitable for younger children. [familyinfo...ire.gov.uk]
https://www.natgeokids.com/uk/

pageCache.pageTitle: Firle Church of England Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages
pageCache.text:
Learning
Modern Foreign Languages
At Laughton Community Primary School and Firle Church of England Primary School our MFL curriculum is designed to inspire children’s learning for life. We believe that learning a foreign language is a necessary part of being a member of a multi-cultural society and provides an opening to other cultures. Through high-quality MFL education we aim to foster children’s curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world. We are committed to ensuring that through learning new languages children are enabled to interpret, create and exchange meaning within and across cultures. We want to prepare all our young people to have the confidence to participate in the rapidly changing world in which we live and provide the foundation to ensure pupils develop an interest in and thirst for learning other languages in the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Firle Church of England Primary School - Maths
pageCache.text:
Learning
Maths
Oaktree Federation Mathematics Intent
At The Oak Tree Federation our Mathematics curriculum is designed in line with our vision to inspire children’s learning for life. The federation has adopted the mastery approach with the intent that children acquire a deep, long-term, secure and adaptable understanding of the subject. The aim is to use the five big ideas of mastery to inspire all learners to develop their subject knowledge and mathematical skills. The aim is for children to feel confident in using the mastery approach in mathematics.

pageCache.pageTitle: Firle Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Learning
Music
Our intent is for music to be seen as a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. Within the Oaktree Federation, we are dedicated to creating an enjoyable and engaging experience of music for all children. By encouraging the children to participate in a variety of musical experiences, we are actively increasing their creativity, self-confidence and sense of achievement, whilst at the same time, allowing all pupils to develop their love of music.
We aim to provide a music curriculum, which will enable each child to be successful in reaching their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Firle Church of England Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our School
Our Governors
Firle Church of England Primary School and Laughton Primary School have one governing body. Throughout the school year we update our parents/carers, staff and community with the main items we are working on and invite you to ask questions or to find out more.
All schools in England are required by law to have a Governing Board. We are volunteers who work with the Federation’s senior leaders to help ensure that children are receiving the best education they can while they are at school. We support the school by helping to formulate clear aims and objectives for improving our two schools and look at data and other results to see how well we have done and what could be further improved.
We meet as a whole group six times a year and we have smaller working groups to focus on specific areas. Individual governors are also ‘ link governors’ with specific responsibility for areas of the federation improvement plan. The details of our working groups and link governors can be found below.
